A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JAFAR and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated supplementary content and renumbered efficiency tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, depth estimation, CAM, BeV, and ablation results, plus supplementary checkpoint comparisons and runtime/memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original downstream experiments and additional SFT-removal, upsampling-scale, RoPE, attention-map, and BeV efficiency results.

M1.justification: The shared image representation, SFT-modulated keys, RoPE, attention mechanism, and training objective are retained. Component-removal experiments are ablations, and Figure 2's Encoder-to-Projector labels are renaming. The optional distillation comparison already appears in v1.

E1.justification: The training data and downstream task coverage are retained. v2 names nuScenes for the existing BeV experiment rather than establishing an added dataset evaluation. The new scale and component analyses use existing Cityscapes/VOC coverage.

E2.justification: LoftUp, already evaluated elsewhere in v1, joins the BeV resource comparison in v2 Table 14 with memory and GFLOPs measurements; its BeV mIoU is unreported. The existing downstream accuracy comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 adds resolution sweeps spanning input grids of 8×8–32×32 and outputs of 56×56–896×896, SFT/RoPE removal controls, and BeV resource measurements. Section 4.3.5 also revises the stated no-upsampling image resolution from 496×224 to 224×476. This establishes a reported setting change, without establishing that the retained BeV results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's key-generation and attention-head ablations, v2 adds direct SFT removal in Table 5, extreme-scale robustness in Table 10, RoPE ablation in Table 11, attention-map case studies in Figure 9, and BeV efficiency analysis in Table 14. These substantially expand examination of the architecture's mechanisms and scaling behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. The new results retain point-estimate reporting; the standard deviation in the unchanged CAM correlation formula is not run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries are retained, while substantial new ablation, scale-sweep, and resource results appear. For example, v2 Table 5 adds Cityscapes mIoU 56.53 without SFT versus 61.47 with SFT; Table 11 reports 36.09 without RoPE versus 60.86 with RoPE at 448×448. Table 14 adds BeV memory/GFLOPs while repeating existing BeV accuracy values.

T1.justification: The attention, loss, and CAM metric definitions retain their mathematical substance, with no new formal results or proofs. Equation (2) replaces the multiplication dot with an explicit elementwise symbol, clarifying the already described feature-wise SFT operation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of lightweight, task-agnostic, arbitrary-resolution feature upsampling and generalization from low-resolution training. The added analyses support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix B.5 interprets attention concentration as supporting potentially localized attention while retaining a broad receptive field. Appendix F newly identifies prohibitive computation and memory for large key grids, such as 64×64 or higher. Appendix E adds an accuracy–computation tradeoff discussion; v1's separate-per-backbone training limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 4.3.5 newly identifies nuScenes and revises the reported BeV image dimensions. Section 4.4 clarifies that the linear-projection ablation matches JAFAR's embedding dimension. Existing optimizer, training-budget, hardware, baseline-implementation, and access information is otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the nuScenes reference and cites Swin Transformer, Generalized Neighborhood Attention, and Slide-Transformer as possible localized-attention directions. The positioning against LiFT, FeatUp, and LoftUp remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to modulation explanations, ablation prose, terminology, and cross-references. v2 adds an affiliation and acknowledgments, updates the publication header, and groups the former CAM and baseline appendices under Additional Details. Most main-text prose is retained; Appendix C.1 introduces incorrect references to Tables 8 and 10 instead of 7 and 8.

P2.justification: Figure 2's labels and illustrative feature maps are revised. v2 adds attention-map Figure 9 and Tables 10, 11, and 14, extends Table 5, and adjusts table headers and formatting. Existing qualitative comparison panels remain, with supplementary figures and tables relocated within the retained overall layout.

improvement.justification: v1's broad empirical evidence is retained, while v2's direct component ablations and scale sweep strengthen support for the existing design and generalization claims. Resource measurements and Appendix F clarify practical limits. These focused gains outweigh minor reporting defects, including C.1's incorrect table references and the claimed 3–10% GFLOPs overhead despite Table 14 implying approximately 11.1% for PointBeV.
